claims.claim: Easter Island's statues may have walked to their platforms.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: abstract, 1, 1.1, Fig. 12 caption, 3 (Conclusion)
claims.note: LH25 1: 'Rapa Nui's massive stone statues "walked" from their quarry to ceremonial platforms'; abstract: 'designed for transport vertically in a controlled "walking" motion'. 'May have' is the needed hedge: LH25 1 says 'some scholars continue to reject the walking hypothesis', and its Conclusion allows that small moai (under 2 m) could have been moved horizontally. 'To their platforms' scopes it to the statues that reached platforms: LH25 counts 318 bedrock quarry moai (Fig. 12 caption) that never left the quarry, so an unscoped 'walked' would overreach; as a hedged generic about statues and their platforms it does not. 'Walked' is the paper's own term; sentence 6 says what it means.

claims.claim: And when they arrived, two archaeologists say, they were reshaped to stand still.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: author block, 1.1, Pavel passage, 2.4
claims.note: 'They' = the statues that walked to their platforms (sentence 1), i.e. platform statues; LH25 claims reshaping only for ahu moai. 1.1: 'Platform moai, once they reached their destinations, were substantially modified through base reshaping to eliminate this lean'; 'This modification occurred after transport'. 'Stand still' is the paper's phrase: Pavel 'was trying to walk a statue specifically engineered to stand still. The modifications made to moai upon reaching an ahu ... were precisely designed for stability, not mobility.' 2.4: 'later modified to stand erect on ceremonial platforms'. Authors: Lipo (Dept. of Anthropology, Binghamton) and Hunt (School of Anthropology, Arizona), so 'two archaeologists' holds. The attribution is required: LH25's only direct physical evidence for the trimming is a personal communication (S. Rapu 2011).

claims.claim: The clues are in the statues out on the roads.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1.1, 2.5, 2.5.3; script sentences 4, 13-14; SOURCES entries 1, 2, 9
claims.note: Re-check after A7 fix (previous wording 'the statues that never arrived' was struck for asserting the transport-failure reading). 'The statues out on the roads' = the road statues of the next sentence (LH25 1.1: '62 statues documented along ancient transport roads'); it makes no claim about why they are there, so it holds on both readings LH25 reports (transport failure, 1.1; deliberate placement along ceremonial paths, 2.5) and no longer contradicts the closing question. 'The clues are in' them: the authors' case does rest on road moai (abstract: 'with a focus on 62 road statues'; 1.1 base ratio, lean, missing eye sockets), and the reshaping it points to is attributed in sentence 2. SOURCES entry 1 now quotes this wording and has dropped the 'true on either reading' defence.

claims.claim: Dozens lie along the old roads from the quarry, apparently dropped on the way.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: abstract, 1.1, 1.3, Fig. 7, Fig. 12 caption, 2.5
claims.note: 1.1: '62 statues documented along ancient transport roads, abandoned where they fell at various points of their journey from the Rano Raraku quarry'; roads 'radiate from Rano Raraku'. Fig. 12 caption counts 84; 'dozens' fits both. 'Apparently' marks the transport-failure reading as an appearance, not a fact, and 2.5 records the dispute. Two (Fig. 7) are partly buried at an angle after re-erection attempts; 'lie' still holds for the group.

claims.claim: On average, their bases are almost as wide as their shoulders, and they lean forward.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1.1, Figs. 1, 4, 5. NOT opened: doi:10.5281/zenodo.17329904 (Zenodo unreachable from this sandbox)
claims.note: 'Their' / 'they' = the dozens on the roads (sentence 4): resolves correctly. 1.1: road statues 'exhibit a shoulder-to-base width ratio approaching 1.0, meaning the base width nearly equals the shoulder width'; 'road moai exhibit a pronounced and consistent forward lean, typically ranging from 6 to 15 degrees from vertical'. 'On average' is narrower than the paper's text, so it passes A3 on LH25 alone; the corrected Zenodo figures in SOURCES 3/7 are not verified by this pass and must not go on screen. Advisory: the statues lie on the ground, so 'lean forward' means their carved shape (Fig. 5's base angle) leans when upright; LH25 uses the same present-tense wording, so it passes A3, but 'are carved to lean forward' would close the pedant gap.

claims.claim: Rock a statue like that side to side with ropes, and it steps forward.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1.1, 1.4, Figs. 1, 8, 9
claims.note: 'A statue like that' = one with the road-statue shape just described. 1.1: 'Each lateral rocking motion thus produces a forward "step"'; Fig. 1: 'alternating lateral rope pulls ... A restraining rope prevents forward toppling as side ropes create a controlled rocking motion that advances the statue with each oscillation'. Demonstrated on a replica that 'retained the same proportions and mass distribution' as road moai 12-220-01 (1.4). Leaving out the rear restraining rope does not make the line false.

claims.claim: In a test, eighteen people walked a scaled-down copy, over four tonnes, a hundred meters in forty minutes.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: abstract, 1.4, 1.6.3, 2.1, Fig. 8
claims.note: Abstract: 'precisely scaled 4.35 metric ton replica ... covering 100 m in 40 min with a team of 18 people'; 1.4: 'minimum crew of 18 individuals, four on each lateral rope and ten on the rear rope ... sustained forward movement of 100 m in just 40 min'; 1.6.3: '18 people were able to walk our replica moai a distance of 100 m in 40 min'. 'Scaled-down': 1.4, the original 'stands 7.35 m tall and 2.83 m wide. Our concrete replica, scaled for practical experimentation, weighed 4.35 metric tons', made to the tuff's specific gravity. LH25 never says 'smaller' in words, but a same-density 4.35 t copy of a 7.35 m statue can only be smaller (LH25 gives ~74 t for statues over 10 m), and 'scaled for practical experimentation' means that. 4.35 t = over four tonnes.

claims.claim: The statues on the platforms are different. They were made to stand straight, and on average their bases are narrower than their shoulders.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1.1, 2.4, Fig. 2. NOT opened: doi:10.5281/zenodo.17329904 (unreachable)
claims.note: Re-check after the advisory was applied ('stand straight' became 'were made to stand straight'). 'They' / 'their' = platform statues: resolves. 'Were made to stand straight': 2.4, ahu moai 'stand vertically upright (bases flattened) with their center of mass positioned stably over their base' and were 'modified to stand erect on ceremonial platforms'; 1.1, 'to achieve stable upright positioning'. The wording is true on either side of the dispute, since platform statues were set up upright whether or not they were trimmed, and it no longer implies they all stand today. 1.1: 'platform statues show ratios consistently exceeding 1.0, with shoulders wider than bases'; 'on average' is narrower than 'consistently', so LH25's text supports it. SOURCES 7 quotes a Zenodo correction keeping the direction (1.132 vs 1.025); not opened by this pass, so the claim rests on LH25 1.1 only and those numbers must not go on screen. Advisory on SOURCES, not the script: entry 7's note that 'many platform statues were later toppled and only some re-erected' is not in LH25 and has no citation; it justifies a wording choice, not a spoken claim, but A1 would want a source if it is kept.

claims.claim: Their eye sockets were carved only once they stood there.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1.1
claims.note: 'Their' / 'they' / 'there' = platform statues, on the platforms (sentence 8): resolves when heard in order. 1.1: 'Ethnographic accounts and archaeological evidence confirm that eyes were carved only as a final step after the statue's successful erection on the platform'; 'only successful erection triggered the final transformation'. LH25 cites nothing specific for it; those accounts were not opened. The line does not claim every platform statue has sockets.

claims.claim: None of the road statues have them.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1.1, Fig. 12 caption
claims.note: 'Them' = eye sockets. 1.1: 'road moai uniformly lack carved eye sockets'; 'The complete absence of eye sockets on all 62 documented road moai'. Fig. 12 counts 84 road moai; 'uniformly' covers road moai generally. 'Road statues' is the neutral label.

claims.claim: So, the two argue, the shape built for walking was carved away at the end of the journey.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1.1, 2.4
claims.note: 'The two' = the two archaeologists of sentence 2. 2.4: 'ancestral engineers intentionally designed statues for walking'; 'Once the statues reached their destinations, these transport features were carved away to create stable, upright monuments'. 'The two argue' attributes premise and conclusion to the authors.

claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1, 2.1-2.5
claims.note: 1: 'some scholars continue to reject the walking hypothesis'; section 2 answers the critics by name (Bahn, Flenley, Van Tilburg, Diamond, Velasco, Richards, Cauwe, De Dapper). LH25 records no critic addressing the trimming itself, but rejecting walking entails rejecting 'the shape built for walking', so the line holds.

claims.claim: Other archaeologists think many road statues weren't dropped at all, but set up along the roads on purpose.
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1, 2.5, 2.5.2, 2.5.3
claims.note: 2.5: Richards et al. 2011, Seager Thomas et al. 2023, Cauwe and De Dapper 2015/2022 argue road moai 'were deliberately positioned along ceremonial paths ... rather than representing transport failures', and read platforms under some as 'permanent installation rather than abandonment'; 2.5.2: Routledge/Heyerdahl, 'positioned upright along a ceremonial pathway'; 2.5.3: Cauwe and De Dapper, 'isolated' moai 'not in transit nor abandoned', 'stood for perhaps centuries before being carefully laid down'. 'Set up' (upright), 'weren't dropped', 'many' (not all) fit. LH25 calls the critics 'established voices in Pacific archaeology'; not every one is an archaeologist (Diamond, Flenley), but 'other archaeologists' needs only some, and the ritual-path authors are. Critics read only as LH25 reports them (disclosed in SOURCES 9).

claims.claim: So were they abandoned on the way, or meant to be there all along? What do you think?
claims.where: spoken (closing question; not a factual claim)
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: abstract, 1.1, 2.5; GUARDRAILS E2
claims.note: 'They' = the road statues of sentence 13; 'there' = along the roads: resolves. A question, so the tests are E2 and implied falsehood. The two options are the two attributed readings: LH25 1.1 'abandoned where they fell' and 2.5 'deliberately positioned ... rather than representing transport failures'; the abstract frames the same binary ('transport failure ... rather than deliberate ceremonial placement'). E2: an open question on a dispute the short has just shown, with no keyword to type, no incentive and no promised payoff, so it is not 'comment X' bait; it is the mildest form of engagement prompt, and the owner may still cut 'What do you think?'. Advisory: the viewer weighs the authors' evidence against only the critics' position (disclosed in SOURCES 9). Consistent with claim 3 as now worded ('the statues out on the roads' presupposes neither option).

claims.claim: Hook (A4): what a viewer who swipes away at second two takes from it
claims.source_checked: Lipo & Hunt 2025, J. Archaeol. Sci. 183, 106383, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2025.106383: text extracted from the publisher's PDF (scratchpad lh25dl/flat.txt), read: 1, 1.1, 3; src/generated/moai-reshaped.alignment.json (word timings); src/shorts/moai-reshaped/index.tsx (hook overlay)
claims.note: Alignment: 'Easter' 0.00 s, 'statues' 0.85, 'may' 1.27, 'have' 1.58, 'walked' 1.91-2.30, 'platforms.' ends 3.43; 'two archaeologists' starts 5.72. At 2.0 s the viewer has heard 'Easter Island's statues may have walk-', with 'Rapa Nui · Easter Island / walked here?' on screen from frame 0. Takeaway: Easter Island's statues may have walked. That is a hedged statement of a peer-reviewed, explicitly contested hypothesis (LH25 1), not the popular settled form; not false. The reshaping claim (4.4-8.8 s) is attributed. Not checked here: on-screen labels beyond the hook; index.tsx and the A6 review are being re-cut against this VO and need their own A6 check.
